\caption{\textbf{Box versus empirical shell within each GP recipe, and the support $\times$ acquisition-maximization factorial.} Both versions of a recipe use the same GP constructor. Box inputs are rescaled per coordinate, shell inputs are raw. Top: the shell version of each GP (qLogEI, candidate-set argmax on the shell) against its box version ($[p_{01},p_{99}]$, rescaled to $[0,1]^D$). The rows use one matched set of $n=440$ cells. The two versions differ in support \emph{and} in the acquisition maximizer. For $\ell_0=0.1\sqrt{D}$, the box version uses analytic LogEI with sample-around-best, the acquisition call of MSR. This row therefore also differs in the acquisition. $p_{\mathrm{BH}}$ (cells) is the cell-level Wilcoxon test and $p_{\mathrm{task}}^{\mathrm{BH}}$ the exact task-level Wilcoxon test. Both are corrected by Benjamini--Hochberg over these 3 rows. Tasks = tasks, of the 11, on which the shell version has the higher mean. Bottom: the 2$\times$2 factorial (runs for this version). Continuous maximization is L-BFGS-B on both supports (on the shell over a direction mapped to the shell). The matched set of the four cells has $n=440$. Each of the five factorial contrasts is tested by the exact two-sided Wilcoxon test on the 11 per-task mean differences. The tests are corrected by Benjamini--Hochberg within the five factorial contrasts. Tasks = tasks with a positive contrast. The 95\,\% interval is a percentile bootstrap over tasks. The cell-level $p$ and $d$ are secondary. Means are means of per-task means over completed cells, as in Table~\ref{tab:main}. $\Delta$ of the factorial contrasts is the mean of per-task means. Bold, in both blocks: $p_{\mathrm{task}}^{\mathrm{BH}}<0.05$ within the block's family.}
\label{tab:boxsphere}
